title: Peripheral artery disease: stage, side and ulcer
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's peripheral artery disease and any related ulcer.
note:
Chief Complaint
Non-healing ulcer on right foot.

HPI
Pt is a 61-year-old male presenting for f/u of a chronic ulceration on the top of the right foot. Pt reports the wound has not shown significant improvement over the last month despite local wound care. He denies acute fever or chills. Hx of atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries.

Medication List
- Aspirin 81mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40mg daily

Exam
General: Alert, oriented, in no acute distress.
Right lower extremity: Atherosclerotic changes noted. Non-healing ulcer located on the dorsal surface of the right foot. Wound bed shows granulation tissue with moderate drainage. No signs of systemic infection. Pulses: Pedis weak. Capillary refill 3s.

Assessment
1. Atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries.
2. Ulcer on the right foot.

Plan
- Continue current wound care regimen.
- Debridement scheduled for next week.
- Monitor for signs of infection.
- F/u in 2 weeks.

Electronically signed,
K. Nguyen, DO
05/14/2026
explanations: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the right leg with ulceration of the foot (HCC 263), plus the ulcer code: I70.235.
I70.23- says to use an additional code for the ulcer's site and severity: L97.519 (other part of right foot, severity not documented).

distractors.why: Ulceration is documented: it is the highest stage (HCC 263).
Use an additional code (L97.-) to identify the ulcer.

hccs.label: Atherosclerosis of Arteries of the Extremities with Ulceration or Gangrene

dropped.label: Chronic Ulcer of Skin/Except Pressure/Not Specified as Through to Bone or Muscle
